items.question: How much x402 activity is real commerce?
items.context: Raw counters, Visa and Artemis adjusted figures and academic counts disagree by an order of magnitude, and the x402.org counter has not visibly moved since 2026-08-25. A shared, published method for labeling organic payments does not exist yet.

items.question: Will a2a-x402 be updated for AP2 v0.2?
items.context: The a2a-x402 v0.2 embedded flow puts requirements in an AP2 v0.1 CartMandate, which AP2 v0.2 no longer has. The two transport specs also use different extension URIs.

items.question: Can payment and delivery be made atomic?
items.context: Each payment flow shifts risk to one side. A402 proposes Atomic Service Channels; auth-capture adds refunds but not proof of delivery.

items.question: How decentralized will facilitation be in practice?
items.context: Anyone can run a facilitator, yet most payments go through one, and new products such as the Cloudflare Monetization Gateway also route through it. Facilitator safety rules from research are not part of the spec.

items.question: What will the identity, tax and card-acceptance working groups produce?
items.context: The x402 Foundation has wg-identity, wg-tax, wg-card-acceptance and wg-domain-discovery repositories, but no specification text from them yet.

items.question: Will SDK parity catch up?
items.context: TypeScript covers 13 network families; Python lacks auth-capture and Solana batch-settlement; offer-receipt is TypeScript only; the Java module is unpublished; x402-a2a is not on PyPI.

items.question: Should payment metadata be minimized by the spec?
items.context: Resource URLs and descriptions reach facilitators that may not have data agreements with payers; research proposes filtering middleware, but the spec has no rule.

items.question: Will the GitHub advisories get CVE identifiers, and will reporting move to the foundation?
items.context: Neither high-severity advisory has a CVE id, and SECURITY.md still routes reports to Coinbase's HackerOne program.
